evidence: [sec_0006] However, representing cells as plain text gene sentences offers only shallow signals, since the language decoder is not pretrained on such inputs and cannot fully exploit hidden biological patterns encoded in the data.

summary: The authors favor gene-level embeddings because they preserve biological detail that cell-level pooling would lose.
evidence: [sec_0009] Instead of compressing each cell into a single embedding vector, which would lose important biological nuances, we extract individual embeddings for each gene within the cell.

summary: Cell-level pooling is presented as an inferior alternative because it compresses away biological nuances.
evidence: [sec_0009] Instead of compressing each cell into a single embedding vector, which would lose important biological nuances, we extract individual embeddings for each gene within the cell.

summary: Gene-level embeddings preserve granular transcriptional information and provide the language model with a richer representation.
evidence: [sec_0009] This gene-level approach offers several advantages: it preserves the granular transcriptional information that distinguishes different cell types and states, and it provides our downstream language model with a richer, more detailed representation of the single cell.

summary: The authors select Geneformer because pretraining on single-cell genomics enables it to capture complex gene relationships.
evidence: [sec_0009] We chose Geneformer (Theodoris et al., 2023b; Chen et al., 2024), a transformer-based model pre-trained specifically on single-cell genomics data on masked gene prediction task, as our cell encoder due to its proven ability to capture the complex relationships between genes.

summary: Virtual KG tokens provide structured biological context with compact sequence overhead.
evidence: [sec_0003] A lightweight heterogeneous graph encoder maps a curated 62,507-node biomedical KG (genes, proteins, GO terms, drugs, pathways; 11 relation types) into compact virtual tokens prepended to each cell sentence.

summary: The graph is connected to the language model through projected virtual tokens while retaining a text interface.
evidence: [sec_0010] The LM never reads the graph as text; instead, for each gene g ( i ) in a cell sentence we read its row e g ( i ) ∈ R 256 from E and lift it into the 5120dim LM hidden space with a small KGProjector MLP

summary: Prefix virtual tokens avoid the context-budget cost of representing graph triples as text.
evidence: [sec_0010] without consuming the context budget that a textual triple dump would.

summary: Ranked gene symbols can be read directly by a language-model tokenizer.
evidence: [sec_0003] Each cell is encoded as a Cell Sentence [Levine et al., 2024]: a ranked list of HGNC gene symbols that any LM tokeniser can read directly.

summary: The authors motivate ranked gene symbols through their strong relationship with log-expression and recoverability of expression magnitudes.
evidence: [sec_0007] Rank correlates almost linearly with log-expression ( R 2 ≈ 0 . 90 ), so a lightweight inversion MLP can recover expression magnitudes from a predicted rank list when needed.

summary: The two-layer projector is intended to interpolate from the compact structured KG manifold into the higher-dimensional language-model space.
evidence: [sec_0010] The two-layer design (rather than a single linear 256 → 5120 projection) is motivated by the need to interpolate from the compact, geometrically structured KG manifold into the much higher-dimensional LM hidden space

summary: The static KG requires rerunning KG training to incorporate novel gene-disease associations.
evidence: [sec_0028] First, the KG is a static snapshot; novel gene-disease associations require re-running Stage 0, and future work will explore dynamic KG retrieval.

summary: The input and quality-control requirements may exclude lower-depth clinical samples.
evidence: [sec_0028] clinical samples (tumor biopsies, organoids, spatial transcriptomics) with lower gene-detection depth fall below our 500-gene QC threshold and require further adaptation before clinical deployment.
